summary: Discord is self-serve: you create an application in its Developer Portal, register a redirect address, pick scopes and run the standard authorization code flow. The page read describes no review for the common scopes, and a few scopes are reserved for approved partners.

verdict.headline: Create an application, register a redirect URI, use the authorization code grant. The page read describes no review for standard scopes, but some scopes are partner-only.

wait.label: No review described for standard scopes

prerequisites.detail: Created in the Developer Portal. It gives you a client ID and client secret.

prerequisites.item: A server-side place for the client secret and tokens
prerequisites.detail: Keep the secret out of source code and exchange codes on your server.

steps.title: Create an application in the Developer Portal
steps.detail: This produces your client ID and client secret.

steps.title: Register your redirect URIs
steps.detail: Discord sends users back with a code plus state and iss values. Check state to guard against forged requests.

steps.title: Choose scopes and avoid partner-only ones
steps.detail: Common scopes include identify, email, guilds and connections. Several others are limited to approved partners and fail or misbehave without approval.

steps.title: Implement the authorization code grant
steps.detail: Use it for production instead of the implicit grant, which gives no refresh token. Token and revocation calls must be form-encoded, not JSON.

steps.title: Store refresh tokens and refresh before expiry
steps.detail: Access tokens in the examples last 7 days, and the code grant returns a refresh token.

steps.title: If you add a bot, authorize it to a server
steps.detail: Bots with elevated permissions need the owner's account to use two-factor authentication on servers that enforce it.

limits.title: Partner-only scopes
limits.detail: dm_channels.read, identify.premium, voice, applications.builds.upload and the rpc scopes are limited to approved partners. relationships.read goes through the Social SDK program.

limits.title: Team-owned applications
limits.detail: Limited to the identify and applications.commands.update scopes.

limits.title: Seven-day access tokens
limits.detail: Based on the examples on the page. Plan to refresh.

blockers.problem: The scope you need is partner-only
blockers.why: Requesting it without approval can cause errors or undocumented behavior.
blockers.nextMove: Design the feature without it, or pursue Discord's partner or Social SDK route.

blockers.problem: Token requests fail with a JSON body
blockers.why: Token and revocation endpoints accept only application/x-www-form-urlencoded.

blockers.problem: A team-owned app cannot use the scope you want
blockers.why: Team applications are limited to two scopes.
blockers.nextMove: Register the app under a personal account, or redesign around the allowed scopes.

agentCanDo: Pick the minimum scopes for your feature and flag any that are partner-only
Write the redirect handler, state check and form-encoded token exchange
Build token storage and the refresh job
Create the Composio auth config once you have a client ID and secret
youMustDo: Sign in to the Developer Portal and create the application
Copy the client secret into your secret store
Add the bot to a server and enable two-factor authentication on the owner account if required

uncertainties: The page read covers OAuth2 only. Bot verification and privileged intents are separate Discord programs and were not checked here.
No timelines apply because the page describes no review for standard scopes. That is an absence in one page, not a promise.
Not tested hands-on. Discord is a good candidate for a 20 minute hands-on test.
